summary: Bernhard Forssman is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann (~1957–1964), holding posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and Erlangen-Nuremberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Vienna, Bonn, and Göttingen under Leopold von Schroeder and Franz Kielhorn, he taught at Vienna (1909–1938), the Asia Institute, and Columbia University (1951–1956).

Bernhard Hirzel was an Indologist who studied at Zurich, Carolinum, Berlin, Göttingen, and Paris under Franz Bopp and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich as reader, Docent, and Privatdozent between 1833 and 1845.

Bernhard Jülg was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Heidelberg, Berlin, and Kiel, he held professorships in classical philology at Lviv (1851), Jagiellonian University (1853), and the University of Innsbruck (1863).

Bernhard Karlgren was a scholar in sinology and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University (~1907–1915), where he also held a post (~1915–1918), and later served at the University of Gothenburg (~1918–1939).

Bernhard Kölver was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned degrees from Frankfurt and Cologne, studying under Werner Thomas. He later held posts at Cologne, Kiel University (1974–1993), and the University of Leipzig (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied engineering and applied mathematics at Brooklyn Polytechnic and UCLA, and studied Zen under Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He co-founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers.

Bert Vaux is a linguist who studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University. He held academic posts at Harvard (2000–2003), the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (2003–2006), and the University of Cambridge, where he became Professor in 2021.

Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University and the University of Oxford, completing her PhD under Jonathan A. Silk in 2010. She held posts at Heidelberg University (2015) and Leiden University (2015–2016).

Berthold Delbrück specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Halle and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott, Albrecht Weber, Franz Bopp, and Heymann Steinthal. He was a Privatdozent at Halle (1867–1870) and held a chair at Jena (1870–1913).

Berthold Laufer was a scholar in sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Leipzig under August Conrady. He held positions at the American Museum of Natural History, Columbia University, and the Field Museum.

Bertram Fulke Hartshorne was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Charterhouse School (~1858–1863) and Pembroke College, Oxford, where he completed his B.A. (~1864–1868).

Bertram G. Liyanage works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at Savitribai Phule Pune University (2013–2015), served as Graduate Instructor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and became a PhD student at Temple University (2022).

Beru Khyentse Rinpoche II is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Dzongsar Khenpo Chimey Rinpoche, Kalu Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Bettina Bäumer is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at Salzburg, Vienna, Zurich, Rome, and Munich. Her career includes posts at Banaras Hindu University, the Alice Boner Institute, the University of Vienna, and the Abhinavagupta Research Library.

Bettine Birge is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. She earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University, studying under Wm. Theodore de Bary, Wing-tsit Chan, and Masaaki Sugiyama, and was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

Betty Heimann was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. Educated at Kiel and Halle, she held posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, the University of London (including SOAS), and the University of Ceylon, where she was Professor of Sanskrit (1945–1949).
Betty Jean Shefts is a scholar in linguistics, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied under Franklin Edgerton, Paul Thieme, and Geshe Nornang.
Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and as Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.

Bhadriraju Krishnamurti was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania and under Murray Barnson Emeneau, and held academic posts at Andhra University, UC Berkeley, Osmania University (1962–1986), and the University of Hyderabad (1986–1999).
